summary: The dream of sacrifice. Isma'il submitted. A ram was substituted.
details:
Allah tested His Friend with the heaviest command a father can hear, and He sent it in the gentlest possible form: a dream. For the prophets, the dream is revelation; there was no escape into interpretation. "O my son, I have seen in a dream that I am sacrificing you, so look, what do you see?"

He asked his son. That detail carries a world: the command was Ibrahim's, but he honored the boy with consultation. And the boy, {{n:11|Isma'il}}, raised beside the well of {{p:p-zamzam|Zamzam}}, answered with a sentence that placed him among the prophets before he ever received revelation: "O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, of the patient."

"So when they had both submitted", aslamā, the very verb of Islam: "and he laid him down upon his forehead, We called to him: O {{n:9|Ibrahim}}, you have fulfilled the vision." The test was never about the knife reaching the throat. It was about whether the heart of the Khalil had any attachment that could compete with the command. It did not. "Indeed, this was the clear trial. And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice."

A ram was brought as substitute, and with it a principle that stands over the whole Path: Allah does not desire human blood, He desires surrendered hearts. The nations around Ibrahim sacrificed children to their idols; the God of Ibrahim stopped the knife and abolished the practice in the very story that seemed to demand it.

"And We left for him among later generations: Peace upon Ibrahim." The memory became worship: every year on the day of Nahr, the ummah of Muhammad ﷺ sacrifices in echo of that morning at {{p:p-mina|Mina}}, the rite renewed at {{n:45|the Farewell Hajj}} and repeated wherever Muslims live. The Prophet ﷺ said no deed of the son of {{n:2|Adam}} on that day is more beloved to Allah than the shedding of the sacrificial blood.

Two submissions on one hillside, a father who withheld nothing, a son who volunteered his patience, and a mercy that intercepted the blade. That is the whole religion in a single scene.

quran.ar: يَا بُنَيَّ إِنِّي أَرَىٰ فِي الْمَنَامِ أَنِّي أَذْبَحُكَ فَانظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ ۚ قَالَ يَا أَبَتِ افْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ سَتَجِدُنِي إِن شَاءَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الصَّابِرِينَ
quran.en: O my son, I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you, so look, what do you see? He said: O my father, do as you are commanded; you will find me, if Allah wills, of the patient.
And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.

hadith.text: The son of Adam does no deed on the day of Nahr more beloved to Allah than shedding the blood of sacrifice.

lessons: Surrender is tested at the point of deepest love
Consultation honors even the one under command
Allah interrupts the knife: devotion He wants is of hearts, not of victims
